newsitem.title: GERMANY: Former Opel manager on trial over fraud charges.
newsitem.headline: Former Opel manager on trial over fraud charges.

text.p: A former manager at German carmaker Adam Opel AG went on trial on Monday on charges of blackmail, fraud and tax evasion.

The 57-year-old director at Opel's plant in Bochum is accused of receiving about 6.5 million marks ($3.9 million) in bribes from business partners of the carmaker, a unit of U.S. carmaker General Motors Corp, from 1991 to 1996.
The man, whose name was not released to the media, allegedly placed suppliers under severe pressure to pay the bribes.
He made no statement at the opening of the court hearing about the allegations.
Two other officials of the Opel plant face charges related to allegedly demanding and accepting bribes.
Opel has estimated the damages caused by the workers at about 12.5 million marks.
